answer.rationale: Incumbent has refused to reopen price, so a straight renew-as-is fails the 18% mandate and switching primary at 94% utilization with 14 days to expiry is unsafe for delivery risk. memory_c6 will be checked to confirm the multi-year lever is truly exhausted this cycle (it may already have been used in a prior commitment), and memory_c2 will be checked to confirm the low-cost vendor's actual invoicing accuracy before considering it as pressure leverage or fallback. Intended action: re-enter negotiation focused on terms, scope reduction, and payment terms rather than unit price — mirroring the recovery pattern in memory_c4 where benchmarking and terms renegotiation moved the incumbent without disturbing delivery. A small, guarded second-source test on the constrained component per memory_c3 is reserved as a hedge if negotiation stalls; full switch_primary_vendor and add_second_source at scale are deferred to the next review given the 14-day window and zero buffer.
